newsitem.title: UK: UK Independence party says Conservative to defect.
newsitem.headline: UK Independence party says Conservative to defect.

text.p: Britain's small anti-European Independence Party said on Saturday that a Conservative member of parliament was about to defect and become its leader.

Alan Sked, leader of the three-year-old party, declined to name the MP but said the would-be defector was a prominent member of the small but vocal band of Conservative "Eurosceptics" opposed to European integration and a single currency.
"We have had close discussions with one prominent Tory (Conservative) MP who has shown a very strong interest in defecting to us," Sked told reporters during his party's annual conference in London.
"The door is not yet closed and I would hope that if this person has the courage of their convictions there would be a defection before Christmas, and certainly before the next election," Sked added.
The UK Independence Party, which was founded in 1993, wants Britain to withdraw completely from the EU and negotiate a free trade agreement with other European nations instead.
Two prominent Eurosceptics -- Teresa Gorman and John Carlisle -- both denied they were considering leaving the Conservative Party for the Independence Party.
Prime Minister John Major's majority in parliament has been cut to two as a result of defections to the opposition Labour and Liberal Democrat parties and losses in by-elections.

He could ill afford the loss of another MP in the run-up to general elections which must be held by May 1997 and ended the Conservative annual conference on Friday with a strong appeal for party unity.

Asked to comment on Sked's claim, a Conservative party spokeswoman said: "It sounds to me like someone is trying to make mischief...It's just wishful thinking on the part of the UK Independence Party."
